You might have to take the Editor's word for this one: on the skyline just to the left of the tree can be seen Phil Carstairs' thinning thatch. Will Cockerell has also been picked out in this vicinity by one viewer - but blowed if we can find him now!

Hopes for a team place in the top 20 were high with a relatively unfit Kassa Tadesse and track man Jason Lobo to bolster our team of good club men. And didn't those "club men" run well, particularly Phil Carstairs and Will Cockerell. It was obvious that Tipton had the race sewn up.

Bruce Barton had a fine race after a couple of years of injury and then the scoring ten were completed by Mike Webb and Will Cockerell, neither of them giving each other an inch as they sprinted for the line.

And what about Will Cockerell's fighting 14:12 - followed up by another circuit in 15:18! Our women's team were hoping for a set of medals and looked as if they were going to get them when Helen Maskrey ran our fastest of the day to come in third on leg one.
Concern was shown for Gary Staines who was much further back than we anticipated but no quarter was going to be given by Will Cockerell who descended behind him like a charging bull.

Good to have Mike Kazimierski back in the scoring ten again but the man who is making waves at the moment is Will Cockerell. Another battling run had him scoring at 31 whilst urging on his team mates around the course.

Phil Carstairs was in the 90s and Will Cockerell about 20 places further back. It needs six men to complete a team, however, and battling for that honour were Rob Harding, Darryl Ochse and Mike Kazimierski in the early 200s.
…Kevin Nash who was in turn overtaking Thames men at the finish, Roger gritting his teeth and getting home in 21st - and Will Cockerell fighting tooth and nail to become our tenth man yet again.…
"Come on Kevin, where are you." But it was Rob McHarg next in view to close in our team and then a further wait before Will Cockerell led home the men making up the nine-man team.
Kevin Quinn ran solidly enough while Will Cockerell (deeply into his marathon build up) and Paul Coughlan (later found to be sickening for a cold) ran slower than might have been expected.
With the next team, Boxhill, now nearly two minutes behind, Will "Billy the Kid" Cockerell showed great confidence by moving up and forging a small lead.
Richard Hayman was not looking too comfortable but those "toughies" Rob McHarg, Will Cockerell and Joachim Wolf were running strongly with Norwegian Knut Hegvold also making an impression.

Al Stewart 4th in 32:28 was followed by Mal Byansi 9th 34:10, Paul Smoothy 17th 35:42 and Will Cockerell 20th 36:16. Toby Tanser won over 5 miles in New York on January 7th, 25:19, and a week later was first home again in a 10 kms races with 31:59.

Will Cockerell raised his game to a new level. Last winter he was the only man who scored in all four league races - usually coming home in the late 30s - and here he was on the verge of getting into the teens.
As reserve Will Cockerell said afterwards, "It was almost unbelievable: but of course it wasn't unbelievable at all - just sport at its cruellest".
It was good to see Kevin Nash return from injury in the 3000 steeplechase while Will Cockerell ran a big PB in the B 'chase squeezing under 10 minutes for the first time.

But there was no better example of the team's determination to prove their quality than Will Cockerell's fine PB in the 5000m. Not content with that, just thirty minutes later Will stepped to the line in the 3000 steelechase with 18 year old William Docherty who was making his debut in our British League squad.

Will Cockerell - the man just keeps on improving ! First Belgravian home in the 2003 AAA Half Marathon at Wilmslow, first man home in the National Cross Country, winner of the Cross Country Plate for the second year in succession and now a AAA 12-Stage gold medallist. It seems the sky's the limit for Will.

Will Cockerell has been reserve for us at Sutton Park on several occasions and this time, in spite of having run London two weeks earlier, he made the cut and fully justified his selection by running second fastest on the lap.

Silver too for Will Cockerell in the 5000, who has improved one place in each of the last three years in this event. With the relays to go Belgrave had moved into a small lead over Sale and Birchfield.

Hassan Raidi attempted to go with the leaders in the 5k but faded badly over the last few laps while the more conservative Will Cockerell, bearing in mind the thirty degrees temperature, wound it up as the race progressed.

Mike Trees, Malachi Byansi and Will Cockerell were battling things out in the teens, Dave Mason had started hard but was finding the conditions tricky, while Richard Stannard, not as fit as when we saw him last in October, had gone off steadily but was working his way through.
